properties.name: Every skill states the word a person types, and a gate compares the surfaces that used to drift
properties.rationale:
Anthony, 2026-09-01, asking "I thought there were 23 skills now?" — a question about a count that turned out to be a question about five copies of one surface (`fact:the-command-surface-has-five-copies-and-nothing-reconciles-them`).

⭐ THE PROMPT WAS THIS SESSION'S OWN FAILURE. Asked what commands exist, it answered with 11 of 28 — matching command names against skill names, and reporting the eight aliased ones plus nine others as reachable only through `get_skill`. An agent with full filesystem access under-reported the tool's surface by 60% TO THE PERSON WHO BUILT IT, and he caught it. That is the same shape musicjug reported the day before, arriving from the inside.

⭐ AND HIS SENTENCE IS THE FINDING BEHIND THE HELP CHANGE: "I developed this, but I don't even know how to use most of them (I usually let the agent use them)." If the author cannot name his own commands, the surface is not discoverable by anybody, and a person who does not know a command exists will never type it.

🛑 THE GATE WAS VERIFIED TO FAIL BEFORE IT WAS WIRED, on all three drift shapes and each one that has actually happened: an alias removed (caught, naming the 2026-08-19 failure), a user-scope copy deleted (reported as a NOTE — user scope is outside the repo and CI cannot see it, so claiming to check it would be worse than silence), and a command removed (caught twice — as source-vs-copy drift AND as a skill nobody can type). A check that only passes on a clean tree proves nothing.

📌 THE CAUSE, NAMED: skills are SERVED from the binary so they cannot drift from the running version; commands are COPIED FILES so they can. One half was designed against this failure and the other was not, and the copied half is the one a user in another project actually meets. The gate does not remove that asymmetry — it makes the asymmetry noisy.

⚠️ WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED: user-scope drift can only ever be a note, so the four-command gap that started this can recur on any machine and CI will stay green. Fixing that properly means generating the user-scope copies rather than copying them, which nobody has decided.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
FOUR CHANGES, from one question about a count.

① THE ALIAS TABLE IS COMPLETE. `COMMAND_ALIASES` gained `what-is-this` -> `help`, `where-does-it-go` -> `onboarding`, and `next` (tool-backed). It was missing three of eleven, so `get_skill("what-is-this")` refused with a bare list of names — the precise 2026-08-19 failure the table was written to fix. The original repair covered the aliases that existed then and nothing made the next one join.

② `list_skills` NOW CARRIES A `shortcut` PER SKILL — what a PERSON types, stated by the server rather than derived by the reader. Every skill gets one, including the unaliased majority whose command is simply its own name: returning nothing for those would put the reader back to inferring, which is the defect.

③ `tools/check_command_surface.py`, WIRED INTO CI. Compares the three skill directories, the command source against its copy, every skill against a command that reaches it, every command against a skill that exists, and every renamed command against the alias table.

④ THE `help` SKILL NOW SHOWS THE WHOLE SURFACE, from `list_skills` rather than from a baked list that would drift again — grouped by when a person would reach for one, with the three tool-backed commands named separately because they never appear in that call.

ALSO: the four commands that existed only in this repo were copied to user scope, so the other projects on this machine have them.
